title: Health & pharmacy
body:
Emergency numbers: police 110, ambulance/fire 119 — both free, 24/7, no area code needed. A non-emergency medical triage line, #7119, exists for uncertain cases; expect a wait for English-language support on any of these.

Pharmacies (drugstores) are widespread, but Japanese pharmacies can't fill a foreign prescription — bring enough of any regular medication for the trip. Some common US over-the-counter cold and allergy medicines (anything with pseudoephedrine, e.g. Sudafed, NyQuil, Advil Cold & Sinus) are restricted or banned in Japan; check Japan Customs' import rules before packing if anyone in the group takes one.

⚠ The current US State Department travel advisory level for Japan could not be verified against a primary source this pass — travel.state.gov blocks automated access. Check travel.state.gov directly before departure.
